subject: Epsilon Health: Dedicated GPU pool provisioning + burst/autoscale alignment
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
To: Arielle Thompson <arielle@epsilonhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@epsilonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Epsilon Health Dedicated pool - initial provisioning asks and attachments

Hi Arielle / team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — we're excited to get the dedicated pool turned up for your GenAI inference workloads. Per our discussion, attached are a draft SOW and a concise network/peering matrix. Key asks summarized here so we have a single source of truth for the onboarding sprint: 

- Target region: primary us-west-2, secondary fallback us-east-1 (you mentioned regulatory preference for west but ops would like fallback).
- Initial pool: 8x A100-80GB equivalent capacity (estimate based on current traffic patterns).
- Autoscaling policy: min=2 nodes, target steady=4, max=16 (we'll recommend a conservative start; can adjust after two weeks of telemetry).
- Burst policy: configurable burst to allow up to 25% on-demand capacity for sudden spikes; propose a 72-hour rolling burn rate + cost cap to avoid runaway spend.
- Warmup strategy: request permission to pre-warm 1-2 warm spares during daily peak windows; we can share a warm-primer that reduces cold-starts on first requests.
- Networking: we'll need the network_req_matrix.xlsx items (eg. egress IP list, VPC peering CIDR, firewall rules) completed by your netops to proceed with provisioning.

Attachments: epsilon_sow_draft_v2.pdf (SOW, milestones, acceptance criteria), network_req_matrix.xlsx (simple checklist for netops).

Next steps I propose:
1) Your procurement confirms SOW redlines by EOD Thursday (03/04)
2) Netops fills the matrix by Friday (03/05) so we can start allocation the following week
3) Internal kickoff (ops + cs + netops) Tuesday 03/09 to finalize autoscale and burst thresholds and run a small capacity smoke test

If you want us to decrease initial pool or cap burst lower we can send an updated cost estimate — just tell us the target monthly commit or surge budget.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Senior Implementation Manager
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0182

--
Attachment stubs: epsilon_sow_draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 28 pages); network_req_matrix.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Arielle Thompson <arielle@epsilonhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Epsilon Health Dedicated pool - initial provisioning asks and attachments

Soojin — quick ops notes after scanning the SOW and matrix: 

- A100-80GB equivalent is fine for perf, but for autoscale we should plan for a mix of p4d-equivalent and smaller cheaper instances for burst-to-save. In practice: reserve 6 large nodes and allow burst to 10 smaller nodes + 6 large (gives headroom without full-cost spike).
- Recommend changing burst policy from a 25% on-demand allowance to a two-tier approach: 
  * Tier 1 (short spikes): pre-warmed on-demand capacity up to +30% for <= 30 minutes with auto-throttle
  * Tier 2 (sustained spikes): allow up to +15% for up to 6 hours but trigger an ops alert and cost-control escrow (we can cap by tag).
- Warm spares: agree — we should implement a lightweight warm-primer job that pushes a small batch workload and populates KV caches; schedule it in the 30 minutes before your daily peak.
- Netops asks: if they cannot accept egress IP allowlisting, we should use a TLS outbound proxy and VPN-based peering. I've added a short checklist in the network_req_matrix (see attachment).

Questions for Arielle: do your security folks accept outbound TLS proxies? Also what's your tolerance for cross-region fallback (we need to know if any traffic is geofenced).

I can produce a cost delta estimate by EOD if you confirm target steady-state TPS.

Ben Carter
Capacity Engineering Lead (Redwood Inference)
--
Attachment note: I updated network_req_matrix.xlsx with netops checklist entries (row comments).

From: Arielle Thompson <arielle@epsilonhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@epsilonhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Epsilon Health Dedicated pool - initial provisioning asks and attachments

Hi Soojin / team — thanks, this is helpful. A couple quick answers from our side: 

- Procurement is reviewing the SOW and should have redlines by Thursday EOD.
- Netops: we've looped in our cloud network engineer (cc'd separately on their mail alias). They prefer peering over outbound proxies but can accept a proxy as fallback if peering can't be completed within your suggested timeline.
- Cross-region fallback: compliance requires primary data residency in us-west-2 for patient metadata. We can do compute fallback to us-east-1 for stateless inference only (no patient PHI persisted there). Any fallback plan must explicitly state PHI residency controls.
- SLA: can you confirm the SLA for Dedicated customers for 99.9% per-month availability and how Redwood handles failover across regions? We need to include that verbiage in the SOW.

Also, the security team asked for a short write-up explaining the burst policy cost controls and alerting (they want to see automatic throttles and a manual kill switch). If you can send that before our kickoff, it will smooth approvals.

Thanks,

Arielle Thompson
Head of Platform Engineering
Epsilon Health
--
(Procurement and Netops are on a separate alias; they've been added to the thread.)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
To: Arielle Thompson <arielle@epsilonhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@epsilonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Epsilon Health Dedicated pool - initial provisioning asks and attachments

Thanks, Arielle — noted. Quick summary and action items so we can keep the timeline: 

Summary decisions:
- Region: primary us-west-2 for PHI; compute fallback to us-east-1 allowed for stateless inference only (we will add explicit PHI residency controls to SOW).
- Pool topology: initial reserve 6xlarge + 2xwarm spares; autoscale floor=2, steady target=4, burst cap to be implemented with two-tier approach (Ben's proposal).
- Networking: we prefer peering; if netops cannot complete peering in time we'll use TLS proxy as fallback.

Assigned owners & due dates:
- Procurement (Epsilon): return SOW redlines — due 2027-03-04 (Arielle / procurement)
- Netops (Epsilon): complete network_req_matrix.xlsx or confirm proxy approach — due 2027-03-05 (netops alias)
- Ben: cost delta + burst-cost-control design doc (short) — due 2027-03-05 (Ben) — will include auto-throttle thresholds, alerting, and manual kill switch description
- Marissa: schedule internal kickoff and invite our SRE + Billing ops — due 2027-03-05 (Marissa)

I'll update the SOW with the explicit PHI residency clause and add a short SLA paragraph (99.9% monthly target with defined cross-region failover behavior) and circulate v2 by end of day. Once procurement signs off and netops confirms, we'll schedule the 03/09 kickoff as proposed.

If anyone needs a quick call to resolve netops constraints, Ben and I are available tomorrow 10:00-13:00 PT.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Senior Implementation Manager
Redwood Inference
